subject: Post-call: long-context evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: ACME Product Team <product@acme.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T16:15:00Z
Subject: Post-call: long-context evals & next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned.

Call recap:
- Goal: evaluate long-context model behavior for ACME’s multi-document summarization pipeline (~50–100k tokens across docs).
- Success metrics you called out: summary fidelity (ROUGE/ROUGE-L and custom entity retention), hallucination rate on extractive facts, and consistent truncation handling for streaming ingestion.
- Current constraints: ACME’s production latency target is 500–800ms per request (90th), and you want predictable token costs for a scoped POC.

Recommended models & why:
- redwood-2-13b-long (32k): strong cost/latency balance, tuned for summarization fidelity with longer KV cache optimizations — good first pass for the 32k slice.
- redwood-1-70b-64k (64k): higher quality on multi-doc long-form summarization, better retention of cross-doc entities but higher cost/latency — use for quality baseline comparisons.
- open-llama-13b-32k (baseline): lower-cost baseline for regression testing.

Benchmark & artifacts I’m sharing:
- Attached: acme-long-context-eval-plan.pdf — includes evaluation protocol, prompt sets, and data sampling plan.
- Attached: eval-prompt-sets.zip — initial prompt templates for summarization fidelity, truncation stress tests, and entity-check probes.
- Drive link with raw sample pages and expected-extracts: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3Cdef

Key technical notes / risks:
- Truncation behavior: models handle prefix vs suffix retention differently; our plan includes a prefix-preserving window plus a document-level sentinel strategy to preserve critical metadata (IDs, timestamps).
- Summarization fidelity: we’ll run both ROUGE and a custom entity-recall test (automated NER match + manual spot checks). Expect the 70b 64k to outperform on entity retention, but we need to measure delta vs cost.
- Caching/warmup: for repeated document families we recommend prefix/KV caching to reduce token decode costs and stay within your latency SLOs.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
1) ACME: provide S3 samples (1–2k docs) and a small labeled set (30–50 ground-truth summaries) — target by 2027-03-18.
2) Redwood: provision evaluation cluster and run initial 32k/64k comparison on 3 prompt families — results by 2027-03-22.
3) Tech deep-dive: 60m session to go over KV caching, truncation strategies, and cost estimates — propose Tue 2027-03-16 10:00–11:00 PT.

Action items for this thread:
- ACME (Samir): confirm sample delivery timeline and whether we should include PII redaction step.
- Redwood (me): start test plan and assign Rishi/David to run benchmarks and cost estimates.

Attachments:
- acme-long-context-eval-plan.pdf (5 pages)
- eval-prompt-sets.zip (folder of prompt templates and unit tests)

Thanks — happy to jump on another call to walk through the plan.

Best,

1) Samples: we’ll deliver a small redacted S3 bucket by EOD 2027-03-17. I’ll confirm the exact object prefixes (we prefer a bucket you can read from via a temporary role).
2) PII redaction: yes please — we’ll provide a simple redaction script, but if you can also run a privacy sweep as part of the eval that’d be great.
3) Cost / truncation question: can you call out expected per-request token counts for the 32k vs 64k runs (rough ballpark)? Also curious how Redwood truncation strategy handles interleaved doc metadata — will it drop metadata when exceeding window or prioritize it?
4) Tech deep-dive: Tue 2027-03-16 10:00–11:00 PT works for our engineers — I’ll send a calendar invite for Samir, Nina (product) and Jose (ml infra).

Would it be possible to get a small example report format so our stakeholders can review the results quickly (one page summary + 3 charts)?

Thanks — looking forward to the POC results.

Forwarding Samir’s reply + artifacts. Internal notes / action items:

1) Rishi — please stand up the eval runs per the attached plan:
   - Run redwood-2-13b-long (32k) and redwood-1-70b-64k (64k) on the provided sample set.
   - Tests: summarization fidelity suite (ROUGE + entity-recall), truncation stress tests (incrementally increase context to 64k), and streaming latency profiles (simulate 95th pct request sizes).
   - Config: enable KV caching, use fp16/4-bit quantization where supported to get realistic cost numbers.
   - Deliverable: one-page results summary + 3 charts (ROUGE vs cost, entity-recall vs context, latency CDF). Target: 2027-03-22.

2) David — cost and infra ask:
   - Provide per-request cost estimates for the two model families (assume 1k requests/day avg, and peak 10 rps sustained for 5m bursts). Include both hosted and dedicated (reserved) pricing roughs.
   - Provide any recommended autoscale settings to keep 90th latency < 800ms.

3) Privacy / PII: include a redaction sweep step in the pipeline; mark outputs used for manual spot checks as "redacted=False" only if team signs off. 

4) Deliverable artifacts: attach eval-prompt-sets.zip to the eval runs and store raw traces in the shared drive folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3Cdef

I’ll send the invite once ACME confirms attendees. Samir asked for a simple one-page report + 3 charts — Rishi/David, please make that our default artifact so stakeholders can quickly review.

Thanks — LMK if you need help prioritizing.
